XCorrelationId.description: The correlation id of this call, on every response (CP-API-006).

XIdempotencyStored.description: The id of the stored response row, on a request that was executed with a key.

XIdempotentReplay.description: "true" when this response is the stored first result of the same Idempotency-Key rather than a fresh evaluation (CP-API-003).  The name is the one rest/middleware.py writes; S5IF-G05 fixes the implementation as the baseline.

XTraceparent.description: The trace context of this call, on every response.

XAcceptLanguage.description: zh-CN or en; anything else falls back to en.  Chooses the error message only.
XAcceptLanguage.name: Accept-Language

XCorrelationId.description: Continued when supplied, generated otherwise, and always echoed back on the response.
XCorrelationId.name: X-Correlation-Id

XCsrfToken.description: The value in the readable `factory_csrf` cookie, echoed back on every state-changing call made with a cookie session.  Absent on a bearer call, which is why it is not required: a header is not sent ambiently, and that is the difference the cookie has to cover (FR-SEC-005).  A missing or wrong value answers 403 CSRF_FAILED.
XCsrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token

XIdempotencyKey.description: Scoped to "{METHOD} {route-template}", so the same key on a different endpoint is a different request.  A replay returns the stored response byte-for-byte with X-Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different body answers 422 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and a key whose first request is still running answers 409 REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS (CP-API-003).  This header is the only source of the key: a request body never carries one (S5IF-G08).
XIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

XOperator.description:
Who is acting.  Not required on a read, but mandatory on every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE: the middleware answers 400 OPERATOR_REQUIRED without it (CP-API-002).  Required per operation is expressed by the operation referencing this parameter, not by the flag here.

**Non-Latin-1 names are percent-encoded.**  A header value may only carry ISO-8859-1, so a browser cannot send 张三 at all — it rejects the request before it leaves the page.  A client that cannot fit the name sends `encodeURIComponent(name)` and S1 decodes it back, which keeps a Chinese operator name usable and the audit trail readable.  A name that already fits travels unchanged, so an ASCII `curl -H 'X-Operator: ada'` is unaffected.  A byte-transparent client such as curl may also send the name as UTF-8 directly; the transport reads it as ISO-8859-1, and S1 re-reads those bytes as UTF-8, so both spellings of 张三 land in the audit as 张三 (CP-API-002).
XOperator.name: X-Operator

XTraceparent.description: W3C trace context; continued when supplied, otherwise synthesised from the correlation id.
XTraceparent.name: traceparent

correlationId.description: Echoed as the X-Correlation-Id response header.

errorCode.description: A code from S1's catalogue; see the message column of the same language.

retryable.description: Whether the same request may be sent again unchanged.

stage.description: The pipeline stage that failed, when known.

AcceptanceView.description:
The one answer every step-starting endpoint gives (CP-API-012, SRS 8.1).

``stageId`` is present only when the step belongs to a stage; ``stepRunId`` is the
record the outcome is written to and the id the client watches from here on — a
stage run for a stage step, the artefact an export produces, the provider's own run
id for a forwarded step.  Progress and result arrive over SSE and on the query
endpoint of that record, never in this body, and no field here says which engine
picked the work up (S5IF-G06): a client that had to branch on deployment topology
would be written twice.
AcceptanceView.title: AcceptanceView

ActiveDraftView.description: S5IF-BP05 【裁决】: S1 resolves the active draft so S5 never guesses it.
ActiveDraftView.title: ActiveDraftView

AgentRunView.description: S5IF-INP06 — S1's Question store and event stream complete what S3 reports.
AgentRunView.title: AgentRunView

AgentSpecView.description: One Agent type and the stage it serves (GOV19, used by UI-WB-009).
AgentSpecView.title: AgentSpecView

AllowedActionsView.description: S5IF-G10: the single source of truth for whether a button is usable.
AllowedActionsView.title: AllowedActionsView

AnswerQuestionsBody.description: All answers of one questionnaire, committed together (CP-Q-005).
AnswerQuestionsBody.title: AnswerQuestionsBody

AnswerView.description:
The answer, and whether it was the answer that unblocked the run (CP-Q-005/007).

``resumed`` is false while another blocking question is still open; the run continues
on the last answer, not on this one.
AnswerView.title: AnswerView

actualHash.description: The other side of the comparison: the hash the page presented, or the hash the object carries now.  Null when the page never presented this object.

expectedHash.description: The hash the Gate is bound to — the approval was given against this.

problem.description: Why the two hashes do not agree.

refType.description: What kind of bound object moved.

ApproveGateBody.description: S5IF-FLD07: ``seenBoundHashes`` may be hashes or ``{refId, contentHash}`` objects.
ApproveGateBody.title: ApproveGateBody

ArtifactDiffView.description: S0's diff of two artifacts (FD-ART-013): a unified line list, or JSON paths.
ArtifactDiffView.title: ArtifactDiffView

ArtifactPurgeView.description: FD-ART-010 through S1: the bytes are gone and the index says so.
ArtifactPurgeView.title: ArtifactPurgeView

ArtifactSlot.description:
One artifact a view points at, with what the console needs to decide about the link.

``contentPurged`` is the fact that decides it: FD-ART-010 keeps the metadata and hash and
flips a boolean when the bytes go, and reading such an artifact raises ``ArtifactPurgedError``
(S0 ``artifacts/service.py:313``) — so a download offered without this flag is a click that
fails.  ``status`` is the lifecycle (DRAFT/APPROVED/SUPERSEDED) and says nothing about purging;
it used to be the only thing here, which is why ``_artifact_slot``'s comment claimed a promise
the shape could not keep.
ArtifactSlot.title: ArtifactSlot

BlueprintRefView.description: What the stage's artifacts were produced from: a live draft or a frozen version.
BlueprintRefView.title: BlueprintRefView

BoundObjectView.description: A bound object and its hash — what an approval must quote back (UI-GATE-003).
BoundObjectView.title: BoundObjectView

BudgetSetRequest.description:
The budget statement S5's administration page writes (UI-ADM-003, S5IF-GOV18, M4).

S1 checks the shape it can see — a threshold outside ``(0, 1)`` and a currency that is not
a three-letter code are answered here as ``VALIDATION_ERROR`` naming the field, because a
client that mistyped one of these should learn which one rather than receive S3's own
wording.  What the limit *means* is S3's decision (AI-COST-002), and its row is what the
runtime obeys; S1 holds neither.
BudgetSetRequest.title: BudgetSetRequest

CandidateView.description:
One object inside a stored discovery result (S5IF-BP11).

The candidate list exists so UI-DEP-003 can offer a target at 5,000 objects without
shipping the whole DISCOVERY_RESULT to the browser; ``code`` and ``name`` are what the
search matches on.
CandidateView.title: CandidateView

ChangeRequestImpactView.description:
The change request, plus what the analysis found.

``analyze`` answers with the row it just updated *and* the impact: the stage list and
the report artifact are on the request, the affected objects come from S2's impact read,
and S5's CR panel (UI-OPS-001) shows all of it in one screen.
ChangeRequestImpactView.title: ChangeRequestImpactView

ChangeStatsView.description: How much this Run changes, and how much of it sits outside the managed scope.
ChangeStatsView.title: ChangeStatsView

ChatQuestionView.description:
A question the assistant raised in this turn.

Distinct from ``QuestionView`` on purpose: a stage Question is S1's row with an id, a status
and an answer, and the Gate can be blocked by it (CP-Q-006).  A dialogue question is part of
one answer and is never a blocker, so giving it the same shape would imply a lifecycle it
does not have.
ChatQuestionView.title: ChatQuestionView

ChatTurnItemView.description: One stored turn of the transcript (AI-CHAT-003).
ChatTurnItemView.title: ChatTurnItemView

ClearedView.description:
A mutation that answers with only what it did: a logout, a removal, a revocation.

Typed per field rather than a free ``details`` map (S5IF-G01): a generated client needs to
know that a revoked restricted grant names its classification and a logout names its session,
and neither is a key it has to guess.
ClearedView.title: ClearedView

ColumnMappingProposalView.description:
S5IF-INP03 — the transitional shape.

S3 keeps the structured ``TablePlan`` and ``proposedColumnMapping`` inside the
NRR document and exports neither (S5IF-UP07), so what S1 can honestly forward
today is the mapping each review Question already carries.
ColumnMappingProposalView.title: ColumnMappingProposalView

CommitTraceView.description: S5IF-G03: the ``execution`` member used to be a raw snake_case dump.
CommitTraceView.title: CommitTraceView

CommitWindowSlot.description: The environment's own commit schedule, read live from S4 (CP-WF-027).
CommitWindowSlot.title: CommitWindowSlot

CommitWindowSpec.description:
One allowed commit window (DX-ENV-002): ISO weekdays plus a clock range.

S4 owns the vocabulary; this mirror exists so an operator is told which window is
wrong instead of meeting a pydantic error from the far end of the call.
CommitWindowSpec.title: CommitWindowSpec

ConnectionCheckItemView.description:
One of the eight connection checks, as DX-CON-001 numbers them (S5IF-ENV08).

``state`` is ``PASSED``/``FAILED``/``SKIPPED`` — S4's spelling — and ``detail`` is the
sentence the operator reads next to it, which may be a DHIS2 status line.
ConnectionCheckItemView.title: ConnectionCheckItemView

ConnectionCheckView.description: The eight DX-CON-001 checks, individually displayable (UI-ADM-001).
ConnectionCheckView.title: ConnectionCheckView

CreateProjectBody.description: CP-PRJ-001.  ``targets`` is accepted as the older spelling of the same list.
CreateProjectBody.title: CreateProjectBody

CreateRunView.description:
``POST /workflows/{id}/deployment-runs`` answers with the Run *object*, not its id:
the caller needs the stage list R1…R6 that was just created alongside it.
CreateRunView.title: CreateRunView

DataClassification.description: Overall SRS 20.1, ordered low → high (00 doc, S0 SRS 2).
DataClassification.title: DataClassification

DeleteAcceptedView.description: 202 because the data goes with S2's own delete; ``already`` covers the replay.
DeleteAcceptedView.title: DeleteAcceptedView

DraftView.description: S5IF-BP05 — the transition shape; the whole-document read is S5IF-UP03.
DraftView.title: DraftView

DriftSlot.description: The last recorded drift verdict — never a fresh check (S5IF-FLD05).
DriftSlot.title: DriftSlot

EntryPage.description:
S5IF-BP04 — raw section JSON plus S2's own ``_section``/``_path`` locators.

Those two keys are S2's spelling and S5's checker depends on them (S5IF-BP04),
so they are kept verbatim instead of being renamed to the surrounding camelCase.
EntryPage.title: EntryPage

ErrorDetails.description: Machine-readable context, shape defined per errorCode.  All fields are optional: read only the ones documented for the code you received.  Never contains a secret value, a mask, a length or a prefix (S5IF-G09).

actualType.description: Same pair as ``expectedType``: the type the artifact actually had.

allowedTypes.description: UPLOAD_REJECTED: the media types that pass.

currentState.description: INVALID_STATE: the state the object is in now (SRS 8.3).

currentTime.description: OUTSIDE_COMMIT_WINDOW: the environment's own clock, ISO 8601.

environmentKey.description: ENVIRONMENT_LOCKED, OUTSIDE_COMMIT_WINDOW, PRIOR_VERIFICATION_MISSING: the environment that refused.

environmentTimezone.description: OUTSIDE_COMMIT_WINDOW: timezone the windows are expressed in.

expectedType.description: INTERNAL_ERROR mapped from S2's ARTIFACT_TYPE_MISMATCH (CP-UI-021): the artifact type the forwarded read required.

feature.description: FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED (CP-UI-023): the appendix-B action whose writes are gated, e.g. member.manage.

fields.description: VALIDATION_ERROR: one entry per field the request got wrong (SRS 8.3).

header.description: OPERATOR_REQUIRED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED: the header that was missing.

known.description: AI_GOVERNANCE_ACTION_UNKNOWN: the actions that do exist.

lockChangedAt.description: ENVIRONMENT_LOCKED: when the lock went on, ISO 8601.

lockReason.description: ENVIRONMENT_LOCKED: why the lock is on.

milestone.description: AI_FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED, FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED: the milestone that delivers it.

mismatches.description: APPROVAL_INVALIDATED: each bound object whose hash moved.

providerErrorCode.description: A forwarded call whose provider code S1 reported under its own name: the code the provider actually raised (S5IF-G07.2).

reason.description: UPLOAD_REJECTED: which of the two limits the submission broke.  NOT_FOUND (CP-UI-022): NOT_GENERATED means a pipeline stage would produce the resource later — see ``requiredStage`` for which one; NOT_EXIST means the object truly is not there.

requiredEvidence.description: PRIOR_VERIFICATION_MISSING: what must be produced first.

requiredStage.description: NOT_FOUND with reason NOT_GENERATED: the pipeline stage whose output produces the resource, e.g. BASELINE_COMPILE, BIND_COMPILE or HANDOFF.

requiredStates.description: INVALID_STATE: the states that would have allowed the action, empty when the refusal is not about a state machine at all.

requires.description: INVALID_STATE: the precondition, e.g. ARCHIVED or PROJECT_EXPORT.

runId.description: NOT_FOUND on the dependency graph (CP-UI-022): the runId the request asked about, echoed back so the client can tell which Run was refused.

scope.description: IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS: the endpoint scope, or the step, the key or the in-flight action is held on.

status.description: INVALID_STATE: the current state of the object.

targetId.description: INVALID_STATE: the object that is in the wrong state.

violation.description: UPLOAD_REJECTED: the machine-readable cause behind ``reason`` — a size limit, or a media type that is absent or not allowed.

windows.description: OUTSIDE_COMMIT_WINDOW: the windows the environment accepts.

EvalCaseView.description:
One evaluation case and its verdict (GOV15, S3 ``EvalResult.cases``).

AI-GOV-004 puts these in the detail, so the shape is S3's declared item type and not
a guess: ``diff`` is S3's structured difference, which a string could not carry.
EvalCaseView.title: EvalCaseView

ExecutionSlot.description:
The COMMIT's own record, with each report's artifact slot beside it.

``ArtifactSlot`` rather than a bare ``str`` because the producer already answers that
(``services/runs.py``'s ``_artifact_slot``), and the slot carries ``contentPurged``: a report
whose bytes are gone under the retention rule must not be offered as a download that fails on
click.  Declaring the id alone made ``GET /deployment-runs/{runId}/summary`` a 500 for every
identity the moment a real execution report existed — which no test had, because no fixture
gave the COMMIT stage an ``EXECUTION_REPORT`` output (S5IF-FLD05, CP-UI-012, FD-ART-010).
ExecutionSlot.title: ExecutionSlot

ExecutionView.description: S5IF-G03: this whole projection used to be a raw snake_case ``model_dump()``.
ExecutionView.title: ExecutionView

ExplainResultView.description: The body is *not* here: it lives in the AGENT_OUTPUT artifact (S5IF-INP05).
ExplainResultView.title: ExplainResultView

FrontendPackageFileView.description:
One file inside the development package (CP-UI-021, BP-HO-004).

``kind`` is the file's role in the dev package (DOCUMENT, CONTRACT, UI_SPEC, ...),
deliberately S2's word and not the metadata package's ``role``.
FrontendPackageFileView.title: FrontendPackageFileView

FrontendPackageFilesView.description: What the project's development package holds — S2's listing forwarded whole.
FrontendPackageFilesView.title: FrontendPackageFilesView

GateExplanationView.description: The six sections UI-GATE-001/004 renders (already present, now typed).
GateExplanationView.title: GateExplanationView

GateRejectionView.description: What rejecting a Gate answers: the Gate moved, and the stage it gates came back.
GateRejectionView.title: GateRejectionView

GateSummaryView.description:
One row of the Dashboard's Gate list (S5IF-FLD03).

The two warning numbers are separate because UI-AC-04 acts on different ones: the
approver sees how many there are, the button is greyed out by how many are still
unresolved.  ``highOpenQuestionCount`` is CP-Q-006's blocker, shown on the list so the
approver knows before opening the Gate.
GateSummaryView.title: GateSummaryView

GraphFiltersView.description: The filter echo of a graph request (CP-UI-020): what was narrowed by.
GraphFiltersView.title: GraphFiltersView

GraphNodeView.description:
One Registry entry as S2's build recorded it (CP-UI-020, BP-TD-009).

The degrees are the complete graph's: filtering to one type cannot turn a
referenced object into an orphan (BP-AC-16), so S1 forwards S2's numbers instead
of recomputing anything.  Nodes are Registry entries only — pages, intents and
decisions belong to other views (BP-TD-006).
GraphNodeView.title: GraphNodeView

InputCompletenessView.description: Satisfied ÷ total, from the checklist S1 maintains per stage type.
InputCompletenessView.title: InputCompletenessView

InputView.description: S5IF-INP02 — an uploaded input plus how far its parsing got.
InputView.title: InputView

InvalidationPlanView.description:
What a Major promotion just invalidated (CP-WF-015).

The approval answer has to carry it: the user approved one Gate and the effect ran
across the workflow, so the screen must be able to say which stages, Gates and Runs
moved without a second request.
InvalidationPlanView.title: InvalidationPlanView

IssueView.description:
One finding in a validation / import / compile report.

``level`` is the single spelling S5 sees: S2 calls it ``level`` and S3 calls it
``severity``, and S1 normalises to ``level`` wherever the two meet (S5IF-BP14,
S5IF-FLD07).  ``severity`` is accepted on the way in — a report or a row written before
the rename still says it — and never leaves, so the wire carries one name.
IssueView.title: IssueView

LlmExchangeImageView.description: A picture the request carried, as metadata — the base64 never leaves S3's call.
LlmExchangeImageView.title: LlmExchangeImageView

LlmLogView.description: S5IF-INP08 — one input's parse-time model calls, plus the status that explains them.
LlmLogView.title: LlmLogView

ManualCheckBody.description:
The verdict is not validated here.

An unrecognised outcome means the stage is not in MANUAL_CHECK to be resolved at
all, which the state machine reports as 409 ``INVALID_STATE`` (附录 A /
CP-WF-019).  A 422 here would describe a well-formed request as malformed.
ManualCheckBody.title: ManualCheckBody

MarkReadView.description: The notification, as it now stands: the same view the list answers with.
MarkReadView.title: MarkReadView

MemberPutRequest.description: The whole membership list, replaced: a PUT that left rows behind could not remove anyone.
MemberPutRequest.title: MemberPutRequest

MissingCheckView.description: One precondition the stage cannot start without (S5IF-FLD01).
MissingCheckView.title: MissingCheckView

NotificationChannels.description:
One platform channel (CP-UI-017): ``{type, target, secretRef}``.

``target`` is where the notice goes; ``secretRef`` is a reference to whatever
credential the send needs.  They are separate fields so no URL can ever carry a
password in place of a reference — a value, a mask, a length and a prefix are all
forbidden on this wire (S5IF-G09 / CP-API-015).
NotificationChannels.title: NotificationChannels

ObjectDeletionRequest.description:
The three things S4's ``delete_objects`` needs, and nothing S4 must not be told (DX-EXE-038).

``extra="forbid"`` is deliberate.  A caller that puts ``idempotencyKey`` in the body would
otherwise have it dropped in silence while believing the delete was protected against a
replay — S5IF-G08 【裁决】 made the ``Idempotency-Key`` **header** the only source of the key,
and a deletion is the one call where that mistake cannot be undone afterwards.

There is also no ``importOptions`` field: DX-EXE-038 submits the candidate set with
``importStrategy=DELETE`` and ``atomicMode=ALL``, and those are S4's safety rules rather than
a per-request preference (a half-deleted batch is harder to explain than none at all).
ObjectDeletionRequest.title: ObjectDeletionRequest

ObjectDeletionView.description:
One deletion execution as S4 reported it (DX-EXE-038, S4 SRS 7.4).

The body is S4's ``ExecutionOutcome``, not an S1 judgement: the deletion's verdict is "what
the instance did", and CP-API-007 forbids S1 from keeping a second copy of it.  ``status``
therefore carries S4's ``ExecutionStatus`` — ``COMPLETED`` / ``FAILED`` /
``NEEDS_MANUAL_CHECK`` — and a refusal that never submitted anything is a ``FAILED`` row with
``applied=false`` plus the reason in ``detail``, not an HTTP error.  ``executionId`` is what
makes the answer followable: ``GET /executions/{executionId}`` and the artifact ids in this
same body carry the evidence afterwards.

``environmentKey`` and ``deletionArtifactId`` are echoed from the request because DX-BR-02
admits no default environment and a cleanup that deleted from the wrong one must be readable
from its own answer.
ObjectDeletionView.title: ObjectDeletionView

OidcRequestView.description: What S5 redirects the browser to, plus the values it must echo back.
OidcRequestView.title: OidcRequestView

PackageFileView.description:
One file of the compiled package (S5IF-BP17).

``objectCount`` is null for the files that carry no object — a README holds nothing, which is
a different statement from "this package is empty".
PackageFileView.title: PackageFileView

ParseOptions.description:
S5IF-INP04 — the same endpoint covers a first parse and a re-parse with a
confirmed column mapping (AI-INP-006).
ParseOptions.title: ParseOptions

PatchModelRequest.description:
Edit one registered model (S5IF-GOV06); an absent field means "leave it alone".

This is deliberately *not* :class:`RegisterModelRequest`.  Registration replaces the row, and
two of its columns — AI-LLM-003's per-model ``endpoint`` and Key reference — are nullable, so
an operator who reopened the form to fix a price and did not re-type the address would have
written NULL over it.  S1's read path then back-fills the provider's own address, so the
console shows a value nobody set and the override can never come off.

``extra="forbid"`` for the same reason the provider patch has it: a partial update cannot
afford silence, and a body that misspells ``apiKeySecretRef`` would otherwise be accepted,
change nothing, and read as a successful save.  A field sent as JSON ``null`` is dropped rather
than stored, so ``to_patch`` and the emptiness check below measure the same set.

``capabilities`` stays a free mapping rather than a typed view, in the body and in what S3 is
handed: the patch has to be able to say "this one capability, and only this one", which a typed
view cannot express because it fills what is missing with its own defaults.
PatchModelRequest.title: PatchModelRequest

PatchProviderRequest.description:
Edit one registered provider (S5IF-GOV03); an absent field means "leave it alone".

This is deliberately *not* :class:`RegisterProviderRequest`.  Registration replaces the row,
so an operator who only wanted to fix a mistyped address would have to re-supply the Key
reference, and one who omitted it would silently clear it.

``extra="forbid"`` because a partial update cannot afford silence: a body that misspells
``apiKeySecretRef`` would otherwise be accepted, change nothing, and read as a successful save.
A field sent as JSON ``null`` is dropped rather than stored, so ``to_patch`` and the emptiness
check below measure the same set — and the contract says so, or a generated client will try.
PatchProviderRequest.title: PatchProviderRequest

ProjectPolicyView.description: S5IF-GOV12 — the organisation policy narrowed by every target environment.
ProjectPolicyView.title: ProjectPolicyView

ProtectionSpec.description: The protection block a PRODUCTION environment is registered with (DX-ENV-002).
ProtectionSpec.title: ProtectionSpec

ProviderCatalogueEntry.description:
One built-in vendor suggestion (AI-CAT-001).

A *suggestion*: the address is what this build's OpenAI-compatible client can use, but nothing
here has been probed against the deployment, and a console must not present it as verified.
ProviderCatalogueEntry.title: ProviderCatalogueEntry

ProviderHealthView.description:
S5IF-GOV20 — what one reachability probe answered.

``detail`` is the transport's own sentence (``provider answered HTTP 401``, ``model endpoint
unreachable: ConnectError``); the credential is resolved inside the adapter and never appears
here, in a mask or as a length (AI-LLM-005).
ProviderHealthView.title: ProviderHealthView

QuestionAnswerView.description:
The answer S1 recorded (CP-Q-005 / CP-Q-007).

``text`` is the sentence the agent was resumed with — custom text when the operator
wrote some, the chosen suggestion otherwise — and ``suggestionText`` stays beside the
id so a reviewer can see what was picked without a second request.
QuestionAnswerView.title: QuestionAnswerView

QuestionPage.description: A page of questions from more than one project (`GET /questions`).
QuestionPage.title: QuestionPage

QuestionnaireAnswerItem.description: One row of the review screen's single submit.
QuestionnaireAnswerItem.title: QuestionnaireAnswerItem

QuestionnaireAnswerView.description:
The outcome of one questionnaire submit.

``questions`` is every question still open on the stage *after* the run resumed, so the
review screen can render the next round immediately instead of guessing whether new
questions appeared (and without a second read that could race the run).
QuestionnaireAnswerView.title: QuestionnaireAnswerView

RegressionList.description: `GET /governance/regression-records` (S5IF-GOV11): the results a prompt version has.
RegressionList.title: RegressionList

RelaxationChangeView.description:
The one widening a relaxation recorded: a level, and what it may now also reach.

S3 accepts several spellings of both halves (``classification`` for ``level``,
``allowedClasses``/``classes`` for ``addClasses``) because its own callers predate the
contract. S1 normalises on the way in so the response has exactly one shape to render.
RelaxationChangeView.title: RelaxationChangeView

RelaxationView.description:
What a granted relaxation recorded.

``reason`` and ``change`` are carried back on purpose: a relaxation is permanent and
org-wide, so the answer an operator just pressed has to be readable in the same call.  S3
stores both; a response that named only the id left the operator to trust that the matrix
they see after a reload is the one they asked for.
RelaxationView.title: RelaxationView

RoleAssignmentView.description: What one assignment did: the role, its scope, and whether it now stands.
RoleAssignmentView.title: RoleAssignmentView

RunPage.description: The cross-project Run list (S5IF-FLD04), ordered by ``updatedAt`` descending.
RunPage.title: RunPage

RunSummaryView.description:
The deployment console in one reply (S5IF-FLD05), built with zero DHIS2 calls.

``changeStats`` is empty until S2 publishes the DIFF_REPORT read (S5IF-UP02); the
artifact id it would summarise is already here.  ``drift``, ``capabilityFreshness`` and
``connection`` are *recorded* verdicts, so asking for a fresh one is its own action
(``POST /deployment-runs/{runId}/drift-check``), which is how the panel stays inside
CP-NFR-03 and off the target instance.
RunSummaryView.title: RunSummaryView

SectionSchemaIndexView.description: S5IF-BP01 — enough to build the section list of a schema-driven form.
SectionSchemaIndexView.title: SectionSchemaIndexView

SectionSchemaView.description:
S5IF-BP02 — the self-contained Draft 2020-12 document, passed through as-is.

The known keys are declared so a generated client sees them; ``extra="allow"``
keeps the rest of the JSON Schema vocabulary intact, which is the point of the
endpoint: S5 hands the document to Monaco and React Hook Form unchanged.
SectionSchemaView.title: SectionSchemaView

SessionView.description:
Who the caller is, with what they may do next.

``csrfToken`` is filled in by the sign-in endpoints only.  ``GET /auth/session`` leaves it out:
a reloaded page reads the value from the ``factory_csrf`` cookie instead, and having two sources
for one value is how a client ends up sending a stale one.  Neither channel is readable by a
cross-site page, which is the whole point of the double-submit check (FR-SEC-005).

info.description:
S1 Factory Control Plane — the only public entry point of the DAMF Factory (S5 may call nothing else).  See docs/CHANGELOG.md for the change history; a breaking change raises the major version (S5IF-G11).

**Naming.** Every field name on this wire is camelCase and every enum value is UPPER_SNAKE, including responses projected from a subsystem whose own DTOs are snake_case (S5IF-G03).  The one exception is a system setting *key*: keys are data, stay snake_case, and are declared as an enum (S5IF-FLD10).

**Addressing.** `servers` is deliberately empty.  S5 is served from the same origin as S1 (UI-APP-008), so the deployment injects the base URL; the API prefix is `/api/v1`.  A contract test must not pin a host.

**Pagination.** `{items, limit, total?, offset?, nextCursor?}` (S5IF-G04).  Ordinary lists page by `offset` and sort by `sortBy`+`sortDir`; audit, artifact and event lists page by an opaque `nextCursor` and omit `total` when counting would cost more than the page.  `nextCursor` is null on the last page and must not be parsed by a client.

**Errors.** One envelope, one catalogue (S5IF-G07): a provider code that means the same as an S1 code is reported as the S1 code with the original in `details.providerErrorCode`; a provider code with a meaning of its own that the provider registered upstream passes through unchanged.  `details` never contains a credential, a mask, a length or a prefix (S5IF-G09).  A derived resource the pipeline has not produced yet — a dependency graph, a development package — is 404 `NOT_FOUND` with `details.reason=NOT_GENERATED` and the `requiredStage` that would produce it; that is guidance to finish a stage, never a 200 with a no-content marker (CP-UI-022).

**Traceability.** `x-requirements` on each operation lists the S1 `CP-*` ids and the `S5IF-*` ids it satisfies (S5IF-G11).
info.title: S1 Factory Control Plane

post.description:
Forward S4's deletion execution (DX-EXE-038) for one environment.

``environmentKey`` stays in the path rather than the body: an operation is always bound to an
explicit environment and there is no default one (DX-BR-02, FR-ENV-003), and the same is true
of every other write in this module.

Why this answers synchronously with S4's execution outcome, while ``POST
/deployment-runs/{runId}/commit`` answers 202 with an acceptance envelope (CP-API-012): a
COMMIT is a *step* — S1 has a Run, a StageRun and a Gate approval to accept work into, and the
engine reports back later.  A deletion belongs to no workflow, so S1 has no ``stageId`` or
``stepRunId`` to hand out; promising a 202 whose identifiers it cannot name would send the
caller to a resource that does not exist.  The environment-scoped writes beside this one
(``test-connection``, ``probe-capabilities``) already answer with what the provider said, and
the execution id in this body is the observable handle from here — ``GET
/executions/{executionId}`` and the SSE stream carry the rest (S5IF-G03).

The key is mandatory rather than derived: an irreversible call must not inherit a key S1
invented from the environment and the operator, because the second, different deletion by the
same hand would then be answered with the first one's verdict (NFR-REL-003).  ``operator``
comes from ``X-Operator`` (CP-API-002) and never from the body.

can otherwise see (the provider real/fake mode and ``validate_runtime``'s problems).  A caller
who may not read governance gets ``intelligence: null`` rather than a zero.

Kept off ``GET /settings`` because that one needs ``settings.manage``: an operator
uploading a requirements file is not an administrator, and UI-REQS-001 cannot show a
limit it is not allowed to ask for.

``input.upload`` is a name the project roles hold, so the check needs a project to be
answerable: the console asks with the project it is about to upload into.  Without one the
check falls back to the organisation-wide roles it always used — the numbers are global
settings, and a page must not be unable to show a limit because the caller forgot to say
where it was uploading.

post.description:
A reset by an administrator, or the forced change of a ``mustChangePassword`` account.

Self-service is allowed: a person may change their own password without ``user.manage``, and
nobody may change somebody else's without it.  That is the one place in this module where the
target of the action is a permission of its own, because a role that can reset passwords can
otherwise impersonate anyone.
